query_families: uncertainty, confidence intervals, and decision quality
raw data, distributions, pairing, and repeated measures
scientific color maps and color-vision accessibility
ROC, precision-recall, calibration, and decision thresholds
scientific image integrity and image-based figures
alt text and natural-language visualization descriptions
inclusion_criteria: methods evaluation with explicit display implications
high-value specialist guidance with stated boundaries
exclusion_criteria: source whose metadata could not be reconciled
search_protocol.deduplication_key: DOI when available; otherwise canonical official URL and title
search_protocol.stopping_rule: stop this iteration after every maintained adapter had at least two relevant sources, all major display-risk families had coverage, and new searches produced mostly domain refinements rather than new top-level contract fields

sources.title: Graphical Perception: Theory, Experimentation, and Application to the Development of Graphical Methods
supports: elementary graphical-perception tasks
relative accuracy of position, length, angle, area, volume, and color encodings
limits: tested bounded judgment tasks and stimuli
does not establish a universal chart ranking for every reader task or data structure

sources.title: Graphical Perception and Graphical Methods for Analyzing Scientific Data
supports: graphical perception as a scientific foundation for display design
task-specific scientific graph methods
limits: brief synthesis rather than a complete modern evidence review

sources.title: Crowdsourcing Graphical Perception
supports: replication of spatial-encoding and luminance studies
area perception, chart size, and gridline effects
viability of crowdsourced perception experiments
limits: crowd platform and tested stimuli constrain transfer
perceptual accuracy is not the same as scientific inferential validity

sources.title: Ranking Visualizations of Correlation Using Weber’s Law
supports: large crowdsourced comparison of correlation judgments
task-specific precision differences among nine visualizations
limits: only correlation judgment was tested
positive and negative correlations behaved differently
does not justify one global visualization ranking

sources.title: Assessing Effects of Task and Data Distribution on the Effectiveness of Visual Encodings
supports: visual-encoding effectiveness depends on analytical task and data distribution
position, color, size, and faceting trade-offs
limits: tested 12 trivariate encodings and selected tasks/distributions
does not settle domain-specific statistical graphics

sources.title: Task-Based Effectiveness of Basic Visualizations
supports: tables, lines, bars, scatterplots, and pies differ by reader task
exact lookup and pattern tasks need not use the same representation
limits: small tabular datasets, ten tasks, and two datasets
effectiveness results do not override scientific design or uncertainty needs

sources.title: Beyond Bar and Line Graphs: Time for a New Data Presentation Paradigm
supports: bar and line summaries can hide distributions, outliers, and paired structure
small datasets often require visible observations
figure choice should follow sample size and study design
limits: sampled physiology journals and predominantly small-n continuous data
does not mean every bar chart or every aggregation is invalid

sources.title: Researchers Misunderstand Confidence Intervals and Standard Error Bars
supports: researchers confuse confidence intervals and standard-error bars
independent and repeated-measures designs require different interpretation
uncertainty semantics must be explicit
limits: web task used a specific significance-judgment setup
sampled selected research communities

sources.title: Inference by Eye: Confidence Intervals and How to Read Pictures of Data
supports: intervals should relate directly to the effect of interest
visual inference must respect experimental design
overlap heuristics have bounded conditions
limits: some rules concern independent-group confidence intervals
not a universal substitute for formal analysis

sources.title: Error Bars Considered Harmful: Exploring Alternate Encodings for Mean and Error
supports: uncertainty encoding changes viewer decisions
mean-plus-error-bar conventions can mislead
alternative encodings can improve selected judgments
limits: crowdsourced general-audience experiments with selected encodings
no single alternative wins every task

sources.title: Hypothetical Outcome Plots Outperform Error Bars and Violin Plots for Inferences about Reliability of Variable Ordering
supports: animated outcome displays improved selected multivariate probability judgments
joint-distribution reasoning differs from single-distribution lookup
limits: HOPs were worse for some high-variance univariate tasks
animated medium and tested distributions constrain transfer

sources.title: Uncertainty Displays Using Quantile Dotplots or CDFs Improve Transit Decision-Making
supports: frequency-based uncertainty displays improved incentivized transit decisions
point predictions conceal decision-relevant uncertainty
limits: single transit-decision context
display benefits may depend on numeracy, task, and loss function

sources.title: Ethical Dimensions of Visualization Research
supports: visualization design creates ethical obligations beyond technical correctness
display choices can materially influence decisions
limits: normative analysis rather than a controlled comparative experiment

sources.title: The Misuse of Colour in Science Communication
supports: perceptually non-uniform color maps distort apparent data variation
scientific color maps should match sequential, diverging, or cyclic structure
color-vision and grayscale accessibility matter
limits: palette suitability remains data- and task-specific
the paper is guidance and demonstration, not a universal viewer experiment

sources.title: Optimizing colormaps with consideration for color vision deficiency to enable accurate interpretation of scientific data
supports: color maps can be optimized for color-vision deficiency and perceptual uniformity
CVD-aware maps improve access to scientific gradients
limits: focuses continuous color maps and modeled/viewer conditions
does not replace redundant encoding where color is categorical or critical

sources.title: The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets
supports: ROC can hide practical false-positive burden under class imbalance
precision-recall changes with class prevalence and exposes early-retrieval behavior
limits: PR is not universally superior for every decision
metric choice still depends on costs, prevalence, thresholds, and task

sources.title: Calibration: The Achilles Heel of Predictive Analytics
supports: calibration curves are necessary for understanding probabilistic prediction
discrimination and calibration answer different questions
external validation needs adequate sample size
limits: clinical-risk prediction focus
calibration alone does not establish utility or fairness

sources.title: Predicting Good Probabilities with Supervised Learning
supports: different algorithms produce systematic probability distortions
calibration methods and data requirements matter
limits: older algorithm families and benchmark datasets
not a display-comprehension study

sources.title: Proposals on Kaplan–Meier Plots in Medical Research and a Survey of Stakeholder Views
supports: extended risk tables and confidence bands were preferred additions to Kaplan–Meier plots
time-to-event displays should expose changing risk sets and uncertainty
limits: preferences are not the same as measured comprehension
sample was dominated by statisticians and clinicians

sources.title: Survival Plots of Time-to-Event Outcomes in Clinical Trials: Good Practice and Pitfalls
supports: time-to-event plots require survival-specific semantics
numbers at risk, censoring, scale, and follow-up affect interpretation
limits: clinical-trial focus and earlier conventions
must be combined with current analysis/reporting guidance

sources.title: Use of Directed Acyclic Graphs to Identify Confounders in Applied Health Research
supports: DAG availability, estimands, construction, and adjustment sets are often underreported
causal diagrams should expose assumptions and analytical consequences
limits: reviewed applied health research
a diagram does not validate the truth of its causal edges

sources.title: How to Use t-SNE Effectively
supports: t-SNE appearance depends strongly on perplexity, iteration, initialization, and data geometry
cluster sizes and distances can be misleading
limits: interactive demonstrations and synthetic examples
does not invalidate all task-specific use of t-SNE

sources.title: The Art of Using t-SNE for Single-Cell Transcriptomics
supports: naive t-SNE can distort global structure
initialization, learning rate, multiscale kernels, and stability checks affect interpretation
limits: single-cell transcriptomics focus
improved embeddings still do not independently establish mechanism

sources.title: The Specious Art of Single-Cell Genomics
supports: extreme two-dimensional reduction inevitably distorts high-dimensional data
parameter tuning can yield contradictory visual stories
embeddings should not carry unsupported quantitative or mechanistic inference
limits: strong critique centered on single-cell genomics
other domains and bounded orientation tasks may differ

sources.title: What’s in a Picture? The Temptation of Image Manipulation
supports: retain original image data
global adjustments and composites require disclosure and consistency
selective alteration or representative-image manipulation is unacceptable
limits: cell-biology image examples and 2004 tooling context
exact venue rules and modality-specific standards still vary

sources.title: Avoiding Twisted Pixels: Ethical Guidelines for Scientific Digital Images
supports: scientific image processing needs ethical boundaries and auditability
image adjustment must preserve meaning
limits: guidance rather than a controlled validation study
modality-specific acquisition standards remain necessary

sources.title: Creating Clear and Informative Image-Based Figures for Scientific Publications
supports: published image figures often lack scale, accessible colors, annotations, and explanations
representative images need legibility and traceable quantitative context
limits: sampled three biology fields and selected journals
findings may not transfer unchanged to every imaging domain

sources.title: Toward Supporting Quality Alt Text in Computing Publications
supports: scientific alt text has distinctive authoring challenges
captions and alt text serve overlapping but non-identical functions
limits: HCI publication sample and ten interviews
does not define one universal scientific alt-text template

sources.title: Accessible Visualization via Natural Language Descriptions: A Four-Level Model of Semantic Content
supports: visualization descriptions can cover construction, statistical relations, perceptual patterns, and domain insights
blind and sighted readers may need different semantic access
limits: bounded corpus and participant sample
the four-level model is not a substitute for user testing or long descriptions

sources.title: Ten Simple Rules for Better Figures
supports: define audience and message before design
clarity and reproducibility outrank decoration
color, tools, and caption choices need purpose
limits: expert guidance rather than a systematic comparative trial
rules require adaptation to the scientific task

sources.title: Points of View, Anew
supports: visualization is a scientific method and reproducibility concern
different data types and tasks require different representations
the field needs current empirical visualization research
limits: editorial framing rather than an acceptance rule or controlled experiment

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.1: Use of Color
supports: color must not be the only visual means of conveying information
redundant cues support access
limits: general web-content standard
scientific figures may require additional semantic descriptions and domain checks

sources.title: Error Bars
supports: error bars must name the quantity they encode
standard deviation, standard error, and confidence intervals have different meanings
limits: short educational article
display semantics still depend on design and estimand

sources.title: Visualizing Samples with Box Plots
supports: box-plot conventions and sample summaries require explicit interpretation
quartile and whisker definitions can vary
limits: short educational article
box plots can still hide observations, pairing, or multimodality

sources.title: CONSORT 2010 Statement: updated guidelines for reporting parallel group randomised trials
supports: participant flow and denominators should be transparently reported
reporting guidance should support appraisal without imposing one rigid article structure
limits: parallel-group randomized trials are the primary scope
reporting compliance does not certify methodological quality

sources.title: The PRISMA 2020 statement: an updated guideline for reporting systematic reviews
supports: study-selection flow, exclusions, synthesis displays, heterogeneity, and certainty require transparent reporting
flow diagrams are adaptable to review type
limits: systematic-review reporting scope
not a conduct or quality-assessment instrument

sources.title: The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Statement: Guidelines for Reporting Observational Studies
supports: observational-study reporting should expose what was planned, done, found, and inferred
reporting completeness supports appraisal
limits: covers cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional designs
not a rigid manuscript format or methodological-quality certificate

sources.title: Reveal, Don’t Conceal
supports: figure structure should align with study design and analysis
dot, box, and violin plots have task- and sample-dependent trade-offs
limits: peripheral vascular disease corpus and primer scope
does not establish one replacement plot for all continuous data

sources.title: Raincloud Plots: A Multi-Platform Tool for Robust Data Visualization
supports: raw observations, density, and summaries can be combined
transparent distribution displays can expose patterns hidden by bars
limits: tutorial and design proposal rather than a universal perceptual experiment
combined encodings can become redundant or crowded

generalization_rule: No source, journal, plot family, or perceptual ranking is universal. Transfer requires matching the reader task, data structure, estimand, audience, medium, and inference claim.

earlier_review_triggers: material change to a maintained rule
